Anya: Quick follow-up from the pinning schema RFC — we need a concrete proposal for how clients should handle a model-pin->variant mismatch. thoughts?
Sam: TL;DR: clients should never silently downgrade behavior. explicit resolver fallback + telemetry.
Liz: Agree. Also: pin id should be immutable GUID, not semver. otherwise we reintroduce fragile string parsing.
Mike: Can we keep a human-friendly label field alongside the GUID for ops? GUID = canonical, label = display.
Ravi: +1 to GUID + label. But how do we convey runtime-compatibility? E.g., quantized vs float variants.
Anya: Proposal idea: rollout_metadata contains: pin_id (GUID), label, compatibility_tags (list), fallback_order (optional list of pin_ids), expiry_ts.
Liz: Example snippet for client resolver: 
```
if pin_id available and compatible_with(runtime): use pin_id
else if compatibility_tags match: pick highest-priority variant from fallback_order
else: surface explicit failure to caller with code=PIN_MISMATCH and telemetry snapshot
```
Sam: + add a permissive flag clients can set: allow_best_effort=true which will soft-fallback and emit a warning instead of hard error. Useful for non-blocking features.
Mike: Ops concern: how do we roll out a pin that intentionally tightens compatibility (e.g., enabling JIT-only kernels)? we need a migration window.
Anya: Include rollout labels: safety_window_seconds and grace_behavior (reject|best_effort|force). Default reject.
Ravi: Telemetry: always log (pin_id, resolved_variant, resolver_path, client_flag_allow_best_effort) as minimal tuple. Will help alert on regressions.
Sam: Also emit a hash of the compatibility_tags set in the header to make telemetry grouping cheap.
Liz: Backcompat: older clients won't understand new fields. Rule: server must maintain a signature-minimal path — if a client doesn't send runtime hints, server should try to use fallback_order and label heuristics, but must not change canonical semantics for pinned traffic.
Anya: Ops playbook item: when deprecating a variant, insert a deprecation_pin that maps to fallback_order and set expiry_ts, then monitor resolver_path errors for 24-72h before hard delete.
Mike: Security: allow pin override only via tenant-admin header or signed rollout token — avoid accidental cross-tenant pinning.
Ravi: Small UX ask: include a short human_reason string in rollout_metadata for quick audit logs.
Anya: Checklist (assign):
- implement server-side resolver honoring fallback_order + compatibility_tags (owner: Sam)
- client SDK: add PIN_MISMATCH error + allow_best_effort flag (owner: Liz)
- telemetry schema (owner: Ravi)
- ops docs for deprecation flow (owner: Mike)
Sam: I'll open a PR with a PoC resolver and unit tests against compatibility matrices.
Liz: I'll add SDK changes to the next sprint, will add a deprecation warning log when allow_best_effort flips it on.
Anya: Great. If nobody objects by EOD tomorrow I'll promote this into a short RFC follow-up and wire it into the rollout playbook. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for rollout-metadata-resolver-test on staging (id: canary-2026-03-22-01)
Mike: noted, will watch telemetry dash for resolver_path spikes.
Sam: thanks — will post the PR link once ready.
Liz: thanks all, super actionable.
